q: Chinon's greatest single-vineyard bottling, Clos de la Dioterie, belongs to which producer?
exp: Old-vine Cab Franc on clay-limestone; Baudry's Croix Boissée is its rival.

q: Which VDN-free Loire sweet appellation ripens Chenin on schist south of Angers, with Château Pierre-Bise a leading name?
ans: Coteaux du Layon (villages like Chaume, Rablay, Beaulieu)
exp: Botrytis or passerillage; Quarts de Chaume and Bonnezeaux are its enclaves.

q: Pouilly-Fumé's flint-smoke reputation rides on which soil term?
exp: Didier Dagueneau's Silex bottling canonized it; Astéroïde comes from ungrafted vines.

q: Which Touraine AOP is the Loire's dedicated Malbec (Côt) island?
exp: Amboise leans Côt for reds; Chenonceaux is a Sauvignon/Côt quality tier.

q: Name the Atlantic-facing Loire region's historic sweet-capable Chenin site owned since 1962 by the Joly family.
exp: 7 ha monopole AOP within Savennières; biodynamics' loudest pulpit.

q: A grower in Pouilly makes a wine labelled Pouilly-sur-Loire rather than Pouilly-Fumé. What grape is in the bottle?
accept: chasselas with sauvignon a permitted minority partner
ans: Chasselas (Sauvignon Blanc is permitted as a minority partner); Pouilly-Fumé is Sauvignon Blanc
exp: Two appellations share one village. Chasselas was the region's grape before Sauvignon displaced it — a low-acid table variety that survives on a handful of hectares only because the AOP protects it. The wine is soft, light and best drunk locally and young; its value to a candidate is as proof that appellation names describe places, not grapes. The same trap exists at Cheverny/Cour-Cheverny.

q: Which Centre-Loire appellation is uniquely allowed to make its rosé from Pinot Gris?
accept: reuilly makes rose from pinot gris
ans: Reuilly (Pinot Gris rosé, alongside Sauvignon Blanc whites and Pinot Noir reds)
exp: Reuilly's pale, faintly spicy Pinot Gris rosé is one of French appellation law's genuine one-offs, made off sandy and limestone soils west of Bourges. Group the Centre-Loire satellites in your head — Quincy (white only, Sauvignon, on sand and gravel), Reuilly (three colours), Menetou-Salon (three colours on Kimmeridgian marl), Coteaux du Giennois, Châteaumeillant (red and rosé only) — and know which colours each is permitted.

q: In Bourgueil, what distinguishes the graviers bottlings from the tuffeau ones?
opts: River-terrace gravels give the firmest, longest-lived wine
Gravel sites are Chenin; the tuffeau slopes are Cabernet Franc
River-terrace gravels give suppler, earlier-drinking wine
Gravel sites are chaptalised; the tuffeau slopes are not
exp: The warm, free-draining gravel terraces beside the Loire ripen early and give the perfumed, supple, drink-soon style; the clay-limestone tuffeau slopes behind them retain water, ripen later and give the structured wines that repay a decade. Saint-Nicolas-de-Bourgueil sits mostly on the lighter sand and gravel, which is why it is generally the earlier-drinking of the two appellations. A grower will often bottle both separately without saying so on the label — ask.

q: Explain the geological line that splits Anjou in two, and give the local name for each half.
accept: anjou noir schist and anjou blanc tuffeau limestone
black anjou on armorican schist white anjou on chalk
schist to the west limestone to the east at the massif armoricain
ans: Anjou Noir, west and south of Angers, sits on the dark schist, slate and volcanic rock of the Massif Armoricain — Savennières, the Layon, the Aubance. Anjou Blanc, to the east towards Saumur, sits on the white Turonian tuffeau limestone of the Paris Basin. The boundary is the eastern edge of the Massif Armoricain, which runs near Angers
exp: This is the single most useful line in Loire geology: it explains why Savennières and the Layon taste of stone and smoke while Saumur's Chenin is chalkier and more linear, and why the region's cellars and châteaux are cut into rock only on the eastern side. It also carries eastward through Touraine, where tuffeau continues under Vouvray and Chinon.

q: What does the 'sur lie' mention legally require of a Muscadet?
opts: A minimum of twenty-four months on lees before bottling
Unracked on its lees through a winter, bottled off them directly
Lees stirring at least monthly, with the wine racked each spring
Second fermentation in bottle on the lees, then disgorgement
exp: The mention is about continuity, not duration: the wine must stay on its fine lees without racking through at least one winter and be drawn straight off them at bottling, at the property, in the year following the harvest — one bottling per lot, no returning wine to lees later. That is what gives the faint prickle of dissolved CO2 and the bready weight. The long ageing minimums belong to the crus communaux instead, where Clisson and Gorges ask for around twenty-four months.

q: Which peppery black grape, also called Chenin Noir, survives chiefly in the Coteaux du Vendômois and Coteaux du Loir, often as a pale vin gris?
exp: Pineau d'Aunis is white-pepper incarnate: pale, low in colour and tannin, high in acid, and unmistakable blind once met. It was widely planted in the middle Loire before Gamay and Cabernet Franc displaced it, and the Coteaux du Vendômois vin gris is its protected stronghold. It has become a natural-wine favourite in Touraine, which is doing more for its survival than the appellation system ever did.

q: Marlborough's two main valleys and their stylistic split:
ans: Wairau (riper, tropical) vs Awatere (cooler, herbal-saline, windier)
exp: The Southern Valleys add clay for Pinot.

q: Cloudy Bay's founding company and year:
ans: David Hohnen of Cape Mentelle (Margaret River), 1985
exp: Now LVMH; the label that globalized Marlborough Sauvignon.

q: Which compound family gives Marlborough Sauvignon its passionfruit punch?
exp: Machine harvest and a little skin contact amplify them; methoxypyrazine adds the capsicum side.

q: Central Otago's bedrock and climate pairing is:
ans: Schist soils with the country's only semi-continental climate
exp: Bannockburn, Gibbston, Bendigo, Alexandra — frost fans and thyme-covered hills.

q: Felton Road's biodynamic Pinots grow in which Central Otago basin?
exp: Block 3 and Block 5 from the Elms vineyard are the flagships.
